concepts.definition: Review at the sprint close boundary under the authority cited by its manifest. Its item classifications and debt outcomes are results; completing this review does not require every outcome to be satisfied.

grounding.quote:
Each classification
takes exactly one core value, for the predicate "the reviewed item is
accepted as compliant under the sprint authority"

concepts.label: Sprint close review

concepts.definition: The six item outcomes are accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice and remove. Debt-entry outcomes are accepted, ticketed, repriced and removed. Each maps to one core value at its close boundary; the repricing layer is a declared change-class fact accompanying the value as domain outcome.

grounding.quote:
Each reviewed item is classified as one of `accepted` (compliant under the
sprint authority), `local_paydown` (local debt remains and is captured by a
paydown ticket), `design_reframe` (the work needs design repricing),
`requirement_reprice` (the work needs requirement repricing),
`product_reprice` (the work changes product definition) or `remove`

concepts.label: Close classifications and debt outcomes

concepts.definition: A durable unit of work with one authoritative record, stable identity and lifecycle. Its default carrier is one markdown file.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is
one markdown file. A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only
when it preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition,
stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal
local copy

concepts.label: Ticket

concepts.definition: One admitted upstream work item with more than one build-tenant execution line, within urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy. The member owns its work-item/ticket-lifecycle relation, while PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 supplies the context and tenant identities; build-tenant identity and realisation meaning are not redefined here.

grounding.quote:
A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more
than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.

concepts.label: Multi-build-tenant work item

concepts.definition: A ticket carrying one tenant-local execution lifecycle, distinct from upstream authority and sibling tenant tickets. Its build_tenant identifies the applicable product how.build_tenants entry.

grounding.quote:
The
`build_tenant` value identifies the
applicable entry in the product's `how.build_tenants` definition; a path
name, display alias or tracker label does not replace that identity unless
the product definition binds it as the identity.

concepts.label: Tenant-local ticket

concepts.definition: The kind of work record. The minimum common type set is feature, bug, spike and chore, expected to suffice for most cases but extensible by a project.

grounding.quote:
The minimum common set of ticket types is `feature`, `bug`, `spike` and
`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for
most cases

concepts.label: Ticket type

concepts.definition: The execution or migration discipline governing a ticket. Its minimum common set is ordinary and implementation_migration, either available to feature, bug, spike or chore.

grounding.quote:
Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type: type answers what kind of
work record this is; category answers what execution or migration
discipline governs the ticket (P3, P1; rc.2 #ticket-category). The minimum
common set is `ordinary` and `implementation_migration`, so a `feature`,
`bug`, `spike` or `chore` may carry either.

concepts.label: Ticket category

concepts.definition: A ticket category for governed replacement of one implementation truth path by another across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces. Examples include replacing tracker/read-model authority, migrating every producer and consumer to a new public interface before closure, and removing a bridge or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

grounding.quote:
`implementation_migration` is
used when the ticket is not "change code until tests pass" but a governed
replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,
consumers, projections and proof surfaces

concepts.label: Implementation migration ticket

concepts.definition: The intake-declared lawful constitutional re-entry class, using SPEC_METHOD §4. Common, non-exhaustive pairings are feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor. A spike remains exploratory but carries its current triage class.

grounding.quote:
Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of
work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully
re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`
declared by intake triage, using the classes of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes)

concepts.label: Change class

concepts.definition: Declared carrier states include ticket statuses, local added states, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and change_class. Minimum ticket statuses are backlog, active and completed. They are not evaluation results and map to no core value.

grounding.quote:
The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes).

concepts.label: Declared carrier state

concepts.definition: Backlog is accepted durable work outside current execution focus that should remain visible; active is the current bounded execution set; completed is closed work retained as history. Product bindings ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed locate these lanes, defaulting respectively to .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/, active/ and completed/. The separation keeps live search small and readable without relocating deferred work into goals or comments.

grounding.quote:
`backlog`
is accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part of the
current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

concepts.label: Ticket lanes

concepts.definition: Family F13 concerns which carrier holds work, what it may claim and when it closes. Instance premises are differing lifetimes, multiple apparent state surfaces, multiple build tenants, migrations between authoritative truth paths and variable carrier technologies. The table presents attributed consequences and separately owned policy choices; it does not decide beyond cited rules.

grounding.quote:
This family (F13 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides which record carries a piece of work, what that record may claim
and when the work closes.

concepts.label: F13 work-carrier family

concepts.definition: One run-scoped contract for each execution governed by the represented method, derived from the smallest lawful carrier selected by work/obligation lifetime after establishing upstream authority. Ticket-shaped means execution-contract fields, not a durable ticket identity or lane state. Contract states include drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded.

grounding.quote:
Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below.

the contract carries at minimum the states named in ACTIVATION §1
(drafted, admitted, rejected, superseded).

concepts.label: Execution contract

concepts.definition: The local gain function of the work: evaluation_criteria express progress/completion and non_closure_conditions express failures that remain despite locally green proof.

grounding.quote:
An execution contract should expose both what counts as progress or
completion and what still counts as failure even when some local proof is
green. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and
`non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for
the work

concepts.label: Evaluation criteria and non-closure conditions

concepts.definition: Ticket and work-instruction terms resolved under PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. Their relevant bounded-context meaning depends on the cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis and affected scope.

grounding.quote:
Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning

concepts.label: Bounded-context work-term binding

concepts.definition: The explicit declaration and live markdown checklist constituting ticket-local authority for implementation migration. Strategy values are inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption; library_usage values are none, consume and extend.

grounding.quote:
A ticket with `ticket_category: implementation_migration` carries both an
explicit migration declaration block and a hard migration checklist. Both
are part of the ticket authority, not optional commentary.

concepts.label: Migration declaration and checklist

concepts.definition: The review of repeated realisation patterns and the declaration of boundary-local rebuilding, consumption of an existing reusable library/commonisation surface, or extension of that surface before local implementation lands.

grounding.quote:
An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local
implementation lands; `library_usage` records which

concepts.label: Recurrence and library review

concepts.definition: A named walk of every live interface able to bypass, reinterpret, replay or project migrating truth, with an interface-specific closure condition for every item.

grounding.quote:
For a core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration, the
ticket includes an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be
used as closure evidence. The checklist is a named walk of every live
interface that can still bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the
migrating truth path

concepts.label: Impacted Interface Review Checklist

concepts.definition: An assessment distinct from construction and owner acceptance. The reviewer is not the reviewed subject's author; a constructor's self-review remains construction evidence. Generic assessment, acceptance and closed-result reuse are attributed respectively to EVALUATION §3, EVALUATION §5 and ACTIVATION §7.

grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).

concepts.label: Independent assessment

concepts.definition: A residual judgment needed by another activation, recorded once with its owning work and distinguished from a direct or lawfully proxied owner ruling. C, J and O are referenced SPEC_METHOD annotations; J is not O.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5.

concepts.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

concepts.definition: An obligation's owner-set post-repricing standing: retained, superseded, deferred or withdrawn. These are recorded states, not assessed-candidate acceptance results or qualified predecessor-claim dispositions, and map to no core value.

grounding.quote:
The four repricing dispositions are recorded states of the obligation,
set by its owning authority; they are not results and map to no core
value.

concepts.label: Obligation repricing disposition

concepts.definition: A bounded claim whose completion is governed by evidence for every applicable obligation, applicable required judgments and owner rulings, absence of active non-closure conditions and any reserved owner acceptance. This member owns the work-claim closure condition; SPEC_METHOD §4 applies it to a change span.

grounding.quote:
A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains.

concepts.label: Work claim

concepts.definition: A proof projection from admitted work authority. A substantive test should derive through ticket, intake triage, lawful re-entry, governing requirement/design/module/published function/carrier/closure surface and then expectation. Implementation behaviour is evidence, not the authority for expected results.

grounding.quote:
ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation

concepts.label: Test case

concepts.definition: One work-state authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, tickets their state, milestone authority subordinate milestones and accepted design realisation decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections.

grounding.quote:
Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections

concepts.label: Work authority chain and projections

concepts.definition: Three recommended document shapes: sprint manifest, ordinary ticket and migration ticket. They illustrate required fields and sections without instantiating the illustrated work. The sprint example carries id/status/goal/timestamps, Authority, Scope, Excluded Boundaries, Expected Change Classes, Iterations and Closure. The ordinary example carries ticket fields, Context, Acceptance and Links. The migration example carries ticket/migration fields, Migration Declaration and the live Migration Checklist.

grounding.quote:
These shapes are the recommended carriers of the fields and sections the
rules above require; a project may bind another shape that carries the
same fields

concepts.label: Recommended carrier templates

conditions: The default local-file carrier is used.
concepts.definition: Humans and agents can read the active folder directly; backlog remains searchable durable work outside immediate focus; rg suffices for locating active work, without a required database or board. Illustrative commands search headings/status/type/goal in active and backlog folders, and T-001/B-002 identities across tickets.

grounding.quote:
The default local-file carrier assumes that humans and agents can read the
active ticket folder directly; that backlog remains searchable durable work
without competing with the active lane for immediate attention; that `rg`
is sufficient for finding active work; and that no database or board is
required

concepts.label: Local-file operating mode

concepts.definition: An attributed provenance ledger routing received rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md anchors to this member or named other members. It claims conserved rows are restated locally and labels heading-only predecessor rows inapplicable. It records new close-result mappings, declared-state distinctions and a foundation table; routes are provenance only, not independent decisions or evidence that conservation was verified.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md received by this member. Anchors are into
rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless another
member is named. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: Ticket source-disposition ledger

conditions: Its instance rules apply where a Product adopts this optional profile.
concepts.definition: Tier-3, application-neutral model-family signature for immutable application histories over an externally changing subject. Stable identity urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile, owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:traversal-occurrence-profile. It imports one exact a_c basis and its laws without amending the calculus, becoming universal to its models or defining a universal execution theory.

grounding.quote:
Tier 3. The `a_c` traversal occurrence profile over mutable subjects: an
optional model-family signature for immutable application histories. It
imports [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md) by reference under
[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of it

Adoption is optional. The profile imports one exact `a_c` basis and
instantiates one closed model-family signature under that basis's record
and model laws. It does not amend `a_c`, does not become part of every
`a_c` model and defines no universal execution theory

concepts.label: Traversal occurrence profile

conditions: A Product adopts the profile and its instance premises.
concepts.definition: Material family F19 imports F3 results/combination and F9 a_c. Its additional premises are I1, externally changing subject reality with a stable binding; I2, Product selection of one exact a_c basis; I3, separately identified effect operations under owner-issued grants. These premises are adopted, not derived from foundations. Cited commitment standing is P0 recovered; P1/P3/P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises hold where a Product adopts the profile; they are
adopted with it and do not follow from the foundations (P1, P6):

- I1: a subject's reality changes outside the model, and a stable binding
  names that subject;
- I2: the adopting Product selects one exact `a_c` basis;
- I3: an effect on the subject is a separately identified operation under
  an owner-issued grant.

concepts.label: F19 occurrence foundation family

concepts.definition: The profile represents an immutable occurrence for one exact traversal application; stable external-subject binding; bounded pre/post-effect observations; intended typed outcomes; separately authorised effects and evidence; immutable admitted framework-event facts; candidate claims, judgments and materialised relations; frontiers and bound projections; and distinct identity dependencies, causal subgraphs and wider typed lineage.
concepts.label: Occurrence representational scope

conditions: An exact AxiomaticCalculusBasis identity b_ac is selected.
concepts.definition: Profile notation Sigma_occurrence = instantiate_signature(b_ac, OccurrenceSignatureDefinition). Neither notation is supplied by the imported calculus. The definition retains the exact finite RecordKind_ac set and declares closed sorts, relation/constraint/judgment/residual/stop kinds, auxiliary values, field reference domains and inherited functor-kind references. The described model is M_occ,b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J), with populations semantic-object→O, typed-relation→E, constraint→C, latitude→L, residual→X, traversal→V, transformation→T and judgment→J.

grounding.quote:
`instantiate_signature` and `OccurrenceSignatureDefinition` are this
profile's own notation; the calculus defines neither.
`OccurrenceSignatureDefinition` imports the exact finite `RecordKind_ac`
set unchanged and declares the complete finite sets of closed sorts,
relation kinds, constraint kinds, judgment kinds, residual kinds, stop
kinds, auxiliary value domains, field reference domains and exact
inherited functor-kind refs given below.

concepts.label: Closed occurrence semantic-object contracts

conditions: A sprint enters close review.
exceptions: Local paydown debt may survive only where its governing method permits explicit follow-up.

grounding.quote:
A sprint may move to
`closed` only when every item and every debt entry is classified and the
resulting paydown or repricing work is durable. Sprint close can accept
local paydown debt only when the governing method allows that debt to
survive as explicit follow-up; it cannot accept hidden authority drift

constraints.statement: Begin by setting the manifest to closing. Freeze new iteration inside the sprint; review every included ticket or iteration against the manifest; check evidence durability; walk changed surfaces against cited authority; classify deferred compliance; open paydown tickets for debt that must survive. Closed requires an outcome for every item and debt entry and durable resulting paydown/repricing work, not universal satisfaction. Hidden authority drift cannot be accepted.

conditions: The reviewed-item predicate is acceptance as compliant under sprint authority; the debt predicate is acceptance under that authority.
exceptions: remove/removed has no matching ACTIVATION disposition.

grounding.quote:
| `accepted` | `accept` | satisfied | the item is compliant under the sprint authority |
| `local_paydown` | `local_repair` | falsified | local debt remains and is captured by a paydown ticket; the debt is the counterexample. The governing relation stays coherent, because an item whose governing authority must change takes a repricing classification instead. It differs from `local_repair` in where the repair is carried: by the paydown ticket, which survives the close where the method allows that debt to survive |
| `design_reframe` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | the accepted design that governs the item must change, so the authority the sprint cites cannot support accepting it |
| `requirement_reprice` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | a governing requirement must change, with the same consequence |
| `product_reprice` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | the work changes the product definition, which the authority the sprint cites cannot support |
| `remove` | none | falsified | the work is backed out or kept out of closure; the reason for removal is the counterexample. No disposition of ACTIVATION §3 has this condition, because removal does not require a violated governing relation or a competing truth path |

constraints.statement: Classifications consume review core results but remain separate from them, as acceptance is separate from assessment. Item mapping: accepted→accept/satisfied; local_paydown→local_repair/falsified, with debt as counterexample and unchanged coherent governing relation; design_reframe, requirement_reprice and product_reprice→re_enter/invalid_basis because the respective governing layer must change; remove→falsified/no disposition because removal needs neither a violated governing relation nor competing truth path. Debt mapping: accepted→accept/satisfied; ticketed→local_repair/falsified; repriced→re_enter/invalid_basis; removed→falsified/no disposition, on corresponding item grounds. Paydown differs from local_repair by carrying repair in a surviving ticket where allowed. Mappings add no core values or dispositions. Remaining debt, repricing and removal cannot be combined as compliance.
constraints.uncertainty: Only the source's local mappings, not the complete imported core algebra or disposition definitions, are supplied.

grounding.quote:
For a local
file, the filename should carry a stable id and a short slug. Recommended
local-file naming:
`T-001-add-product-layer.md`, `B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md`,
`S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md`,
`C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md`.

constraints.statement: Each ticket has exactly one durable authoritative record. Alternative repository/tracker carriers must preserve required contract, history, state transition, stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal local copy. Local filenames should contain stable id and short slug; the T/B/S/C filenames are recommendations, not mandated identities.

conditions: Backlog or active work genuinely has more than one tenant execution line.
exceptions: Completed tickets are not retroactively governed unless reopened or explicitly repriced.
An upstream-only ticket needs no tenant duplicate yet; a single-tenant ticket needs no sibling duplicate.

grounding.quote:
The three lawful cases: an upstream-only ticket (source, product or design
authority only; no tenant duplicate yet); a single-tenant ticket (one
tenant-local execution line; no sibling duplicate required); a multi-tenant
work item (one upstream authority ticket and one suffixed tenant-local
ticket per tenant execution line). For the multi-tenant case: keep the
upstream source, product or design ticket as its own authority surface;
duplicate the work item into one tenant-local ticket per build tenant;
append a build-tenant mnemonic to the base ticket id and filename; keep
status, proof, closure and reopen logic independent for each tenant.

constraints.statement: Keep one upstream authority ticket and one suffixed tenant-local ticket per execution line, appending a build-tenant mnemonic to base id and filename. Status, proof, closure, reopening and repricing remain independent; one ticket cannot close multiple tenant lifecycles or hide another tenant's blocker/false closure behind green status. Duplicates should record source_ticket and build_tenant. build_tenant resolves to the product registry, not an unbound path/alias/label. The unsuffixed base may remain upstream product/design authority. B-030, B-030-T1 and B-030-T2 illustrate naming rather than prescribe actual tenants.

exceptions: governing_library is required when library_usage is consume or extend; library_rationale when none.
source_ticket is mandatory for a tenant-local implementation migration when derived or duplicated from upstream source/product/design work.
Recommended superseded_truth applies only when relevant.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket records at least `id`, `title`, `type`, `ticket_category`,
`status`, `goal`, `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,
`triaged_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at`

constraints.statement: Every ticket records at least id, title, type, ticket_category, status, goal, change_intent, change_class, re_entry_point, triaged_at, created_at and updated_at. Recommended additions are priority, dependencies, links, intake_source, affected_boundary, source_ticket for derivation/duplication and build_tenant for tenant-local work. Migration tickets additionally require migration_strategy and library_usage with conditional library fields; tenant-local migrations require build_tenant. For admission the runtime-drafted contract should additionally carry at minimum target_truth, relevant superseded_truth, closure_law, evaluation_criteria, non_closure_conditions and proof_surface.

conditions: A migration wave publishes/adopts a source carrier and introduces downstream consumers.
exceptions: Downstream exploration is allowed while the source ticket is active, but is non-closure evidence until the source carrier is admitted and authoritative.

grounding.quote:
A downstream ticket may carry exploratory work while the source
ticket is active, but that work is non-closure evidence until the source
carrier is admitted and authoritative. A downstream ticket does not close
while its upstream source-carrier ticket remains open. When one migration
wave introduces a new source carrier and then its prompt, projection or
read-model consumers, the dependency chain runs `source carrier ->
downstream consumers`, never the reverse.

constraints.statement: Source-carrier publication/admission tickets are upstream. Prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review surfaces and other downstream consumers depend on them. Sequence source carrier→downstream consumers, never reverse; a downstream ticket cannot close while its source-carrier ticket remains open.

grounding.quote:
Ticket category and change class are also orthogonal: `change_class`
governs lawful constitutional re-entry; `ticket_category` governs ticket
execution and closure discipline. A ticket may therefore be `type: bug`,
`ticket_category: implementation_migration`, `change_class: design_reframe`
without contradiction

constraints.statement: Type, category and change class are orthogonal dimensions. Record the class intake triage declared, not one inferred from type or category. Common pairings are illustrative, not closed combinations. A spike should terminate in a more specific downstream ticket or an explicit decision that no further substantive change is required.

conditions: Triage determines treatment; the upward walk specifically refines bug classification.
exceptions: Missing/ambiguous evidence leaves treatment unknown, not proof that a governing layer is absent.

grounding.quote:
| the governing requirement is missing or insufficient | `requirement_reprice` | re-enter the requirement's owner |
